votes.plain_language: This vote is on whether the Senate takes up H.R. 6644 (21st Century ROAD to Housing Act), which establishes and modifies various federal housing programs. A Yea begins consideration; a Nay blocks it for now.

votes.question: Motion to Invoke Cloture: Motion to Proceed to H.R. 6644
votes.result: Cloture on the Motion to Proceed Agreed to (84-6, 3/5 majority required)
votes.bill_title: 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act
votes.plain_language: This vote would end debate on whether to take up H.R. 6644 (21st Century ROAD to Housing Act), which establishes and modifies various federal housing programs. Cloture needs 60 votes (three-fifths of the Senate). A Yea moves the Senate toward taking up the bill; a Nay keeps debate open.

votes.question: Motion to Invoke Cloture on the Motion to Proceed: H.R. 7008
votes.result: Cloture on the Motion to Proceed Rejected (53-47, 3/5 majority required)
votes.bill_title: Stop Insider Trading Act
votes.plain_language: This was a vote to end debate on taking up the Stop Insider Trading Act, which would bar members of Congress and their spouses and dependent children from buying stocks and would require public notice before a sale. A Yea would have moved the Senate toward taking up the bill. A Nay blocked ending debate.

votes.question: S. Res. 817
votes.bill_title: An executive resolution authorizing the en bloc consideration in Executive Session of certain nominations on the Executive Calendar.
votes.plain_language: This resolution lets the Senate take up a batch of nominations together instead of one by one, covering executive jobs, judges, ambassadors, and similar posts. A Yea agrees to that group procedure. A Nay does not.

votes.question: Motion to Invoke Cloture: S. Res. 817
votes.bill_title: An executive resolution authorizing the en bloc consideration in Executive Session of certain nominations on the Executive Calendar.
votes.plain_language: This vote would end debate on S.Res. 817, which provides for the en bloc consideration of nominations for various executive officers, judges, ambassadors, and related positions. Cloture needs 60 votes (three-fifths of the Senate). A Yea limits debate so the Senate can move toward a final vote; a Nay keeps debate open.

votes.question: Motion to Invoke Cloture on the Motion to Proceed to S. Res. 526
votes.result: Cloture on the Motion to Proceed Agreed to (99-0, 3/5 majority required)
votes.bill_title: A resolution withholding the pay of Senators if a Government shutdown occurs.
votes.plain_language: This vote would end debate on whether to take up S.Res. 526, which withholds compensation from Senators during any federal government shutdown (i.e., lapse in appropriations for one or more federal agencies or departments). Cloture needs 60 votes (three-fifths of the Senate). A Yea moves the Senate toward taking up the resolution; a Nay keeps debate open.

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.
financial_disclosures.note: Senate financial disclosures are filed through efd.senate.gov, a different system from the House Clerk index used here. Senate filings are not listed yet.

funding.heading: Disclosed campaign receipts
funding.detail: Federal cards show the principal campaign committee and OpenFEC totals for one two-year cycle, plus itemized Schedule A contributors. House uses 2026. Senate uses the cycle of the next election (2026, 2028, or 2030). This is not career fundraising and does not include Schedule E outside spending. Governors do not get a federal contribution list.
